sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page usku1243; TransNewGuinea.org Usku list (116 items, sources Voorhoeve 1971, 1975); ASJP languages/USKU (source Voorhoeve 1971).
sources.note: Glottolog lists 8 references, none descriptive (0 grammar/sketch/phonology); TNG.org and ASJP hold only the Voorhoeve/Galis wordlists, no stress marks or phonological notes.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton et al. (eds.), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.7 'Unclassified languages' (printed pp. 77-78): Usku has 20 speakers; 'The only data available is the word lists collected by Galis (1956b). Part of these have been included in Appendix I.' Appendix I gives ~80 Usku items from Galis in a unified orthography with no accent marks. Phonology sections exist only for Sko, Tami-stock languages, Morwap etc.; nothing at all on Usku phonology or stress.
No phonology section; vocabulary, morphology and four sentences quoted from Im 2006 via Foley 2018; TransNewGuinea.org list (Voorhoeve 1971/1975). Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: Sec. 2.4.1 'Afra [ulf]' (p. 185): first reported with a wordlist as Oeskoe by Galis (1956); further wordlists in Smits & Voorhoeve 1994 and an SIL survey report 'to appear' (Im & Lebold 2006: 250 words, 15 sentences); anthropological report Dumatubun & Wanane ca 1989; ~115 speakers. Confirms that no grammar or phonology exists. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-227 (submitted by Randy Lebold, SIL): add additional name 'Afra' to [ulf]. Adopted 2008-01-14.
sources.note: Name change only (Afra = autonym, Usku = village); cites 'Survey Report on the Usku Language. draft.' No linguistic content.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 345-459. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Printed p. 423: 'Very little is known of these languages, and at present little more can be done than enumerate them... Usku, spoken by a small group of people living south of the Pauwasi River to the west of Dubu... Word lists in these three languages have been published in Voorhoeve 1971.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Isolates: Irian Jaya. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 887-890. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.887
sources.note: p. 887 merely names Usku among five former isolates reassigned to TNG; no data.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU.
